title: Reading Drill — Changing where school buses stop — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Changing where school buses stop — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The school transport committee had been asked to investigate children crossing an entrance used by staff cars in Cairnford. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on conflicts between walkers and drivers, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a ten-week comparison, the team used arrival observations at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because special events might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward an alternate drop-off point. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
